name: GEM
description: In this paper, we present GEM as a General Evaluation benchmark for Multimodal tasks. Different from existing datasets such as GLUE, SuperGLUE, XGLUE and XTREME that mainly focus on natural language tasks, GEM is a large-scale vision-language benchmark, which consists of GEM-I for image-language tasks and GEM-V for video-language tasks. Comparing with existing multimodal datasets such as MSCOCO and Flicker30K for image-language tasks, YouCook2 and MSR-VTT for video-language tasks, GEM is not only the largest vision-language dataset covering image-language tasks and video-language tasks at the same time, but also labeled in multiple languages. We also provide two baseline models for this benchmark. We will release the dataset, code and baseline models, aiming to advance the development of multilingual multimodal research.
evaluation_method: BLEU/CIDEr/METEOR for captioning; Recall@k (e.g., Recall@1/5) for retrieval; Accuracy for VQA (task-specific metrics)
general_score_metric: task-specific (CIDEr for captioning, Recall@k for retrieval, Accuracy for VQA)
typical_sota_score: varies by task (e.g., retrieval Recall@1 ~30–90%; captioning metrics vary widely by metric and language; VQA accuracy ~50–90%)
reputation: A large-scale multilingual multimodal benchmark noted for covering both image- and video-language tasks; less widely adopted than MSCOCO for single tasks but valued for its multilingual and multimodal scope.
notes: Heterogeneous task suite with multiple task-specific metrics; comparisons require care. Possible overlap/contamination with standard corpora (e.g., MSCOCO) and model pretraining data; not a single unified scalar score, so risk of misinterpreting cross-task performance.
